newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shortchanged on diplomatic budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shortchanged on diplomatic budget.

text.p: Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Friday that funds to conduct U.S. diplomacy had been cut to the bone and called on the new Congress taking office in January to face up to the problem.
"Simply put, we cannot sustain our diplomacy on the cheap -- unless we want to shortchange the American people," Christopher said. "But that is just what is happening."

Noting that the U.S. international affairs budget had fallen by 51 percent since 1984, and he had had to close 30 embassies and consulates, Christopher said: "We have long since cut through fat to muscle and bone. We cannot advance American interests by lowering the American flag."
Christopher made his remarks in a speech at the West Point Military Academy. A text was released by the State Department.

Christopher said Americans understood the need for a strong military, but national interest required sufficient funding for both the military and diplomatic affairs. If the United States relied on armed strength alone it would be using its military all the time at too high a cost, he said.

Whatever the composition of the new Congress taking office next January and no matter who was elected president, Christopher said, "It will be high time to face up to the implications of the funding cuts of the last few years and the requirements of future budgets.
"In the context of the need for deficit reduction, I believe we must renew our support for American diplomacy," he said.
